title: Network Infrastructure Eng I, Amazon Dedicated Cloud
descriptionHtml:
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is looking for a Network Infrastructure Engineer to build Amazon Dedicated Cloud regions as part of our Infrastructure Operations team. As dedicated cloud regions continue to expand and grow, Infrastructure Operations is looking for builders to take on the challenge of scaling network systems allowing us to stay ahead of customer demand.

As a Network Infrastructure Engineer, you will work in a dynamic environment to drive the stability and sustainability of our next-generation networks and assist in the development of innovative ways to automate and scale our network. The position's responsibilities include scaling support of several data center locations and day to day assistance with capacity management. Engineers will work closely with internal customers and external vendors to facilitate smooth project execution as directed by Technical Program Managers.

The ideal candidate should be highly autonomous, very detail oriented, possess strong written and verbal communication skills and have significant experience in supporting large scale, enterprise class networks. Excellent network implementation and troubleshooting skills combined with a proven documentation methodology is also required. The desire and ability to work in a fast paced, collaborative environment is essential. In addition to providing top-tier management and support of Amazon’s vast network infrastructure, Network Infrastructure Engineers are expected to build or enhance tools, develop best practices, refine operational procedures and think proactively.

This position requires that the candidate selected be a US Citizen and must currently possess and maintain an active TS/SCI security clearance with polygraph.

Key job responsibilities
- Clearly communicate project status and blockers to leadership and project management.
- Perform device build and cabling validation activities.
- Manage cabling vendor activities and performing quality assurance activities.
- Support Network Engineering deployment activities during scheduled change management windows and participate in the migration (possibly off business hrs), basic configuration and rollout of new or upgraded hardware
- Complete customer requests via Remedy trouble ticketing system
- Troubleshoot networking, routing and inter connectivity issues, including troubleshooting of network device configuration and low-level application interaction.
- Deliver simple, sustainable and repeatable solutions and processes.
- Manage work and priorities through ticketing system and workflow and Collaborate with various stakeholders to remove project obstacles
- Travel within geographical work area is required, up to 40% travel outside traditional work area may be required possibly including international travel and experience with small project scopes and ambiguous details within a relevant work environment

A day in the life
A day in the life of a Network Infrastructure Engineer on our team includes attending meetings, creating and executing change management activities in the data center, deploying hardware, connecting cabling, troubleshooting links, updating tickets, working with peers from all across AWS to innovate and develop, and finding new ways to do it all better for our customers.

About the team
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Amazon values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.

Here at AWS, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empower us to be proud of our differences. Ongoing events and learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) and AmazeCon conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness.

We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Basic qualifications

- 1+ years of network cabling, fiber optics, and test equipment including VFL, power meter, and OTDR experience
- Experience with networking fundamentals
- Current, active US Government Security Clearance of TS/SCI with Polygraph
- General comprehension of the various components and sub-components of data center infrastructure
- 3+ years of mid-level and/or enterprise experience as a technician or engineer; or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

Preferred qualifications

- Knowledge of IP networking fundamentals such as BGP, OSPF and other R&S technologies
- 2+ years of network cabling, fiber optics, and test equipment including VFL, power meter, and OTDR experience
- CCNA or equivalent level networking certification, or Bachelor's degree

title: Sr. Supply Chain Manager, Network Strategy and Performance
descriptionHtml:
As Senior Supply Chain Manager, you will own end-to-end network planning for Amazon's Customer Service network, including outsourced (Global Outsourcing) sites. You will work at the intersection of data, strategy, and operations — translating complex demand signals into accurate staffing plans that protect customer experience while delivering cost efficiency.

You will operate independently, managing ambiguity with rigor and judgment. You will partner closely with CS Operations, Global Outsourcing (GO) Vendor Management, CS Finance, Service Delivery, and Planning Intelligence teams. You will present your analysis and recommendations independently to senior leadership influence planning decisions through well-reasoned, data-backed arguments, and contribute to the team's AI-driven transformation agenda.

This role participates in weekly, monthly, and quarterly business reviews and directly influences outsourcing and staffing decisions across the CS network.


Key job responsibilities
- Own the development, maintenance, and execution of network capacity plans for internal and outsourced sites, covering short-term (4-week), operational (monthly/quarterly), and long-term (3-year) planning horizons.
- Proactively identify and mitigate capacity risks by mapping dependencies across internal sites and Global Outsourcing vendor partners. Communicate risks and mitigation plans to the right stakeholders clearly and with specificity. Coordinate with CS Operations and GO Vendor Management teams to ensure staffing plans are aligned with service level targets and outsourcing strategy.
- Support quarterly submissions to CS Finance, providing accurate Year-to-Go (YTG) labor cost projections and revisions versus OP targets.
- Independently apply AI tools (e.g., AgentZ, Kiro) to improve planning workflows without prompting, identifying opportunities to increase the speed, quality, and scale of planning outputs. Develop side-of-desk automation for repetitive tasks within your planning workstream, demonstrating measurable productivity improvement.
- Build repeatable frameworks that prevent entire categories of planning problems from recurring, becoming the go-to resource when a planning challenge is genuinely hard.
- Present analysis and planning recommendations to leadership independently, adapting your communication style for technical and non-technical, operational and strategic audiences.
- Write clear, concise, and compelling narratives for QBRs, MBRs, and planning reviews. Documents must meet Amazon's standard formatting guidelines, with conclusions that tie to the organization's working-backwards framework.
- Communicate complex planning ideas in a way that is accessible to senior, non-expert audiences. Align cross-functional stakeholders (Operations, Finance, HR, Training and others) to embed planning inputs into execution and operational decision making.

About the team
The Network Strategy and Performance (NSP) team defines and delivers the right human-assisted support to Amazon customers under demand and labor supply volatility, by optimizing the Amazon Customer Service (CS) network for customer experience, associate experience, and cost. We are responsible for: (1) planning customer support staffing; (2) preserving the customer experience when customers contact Customer Service; and (3) ensuring best costs for providing customer support.

We analyze historical data and anticipate potential business events to accurately predict the number of Customer Service Associates (CSAs) required for a given period. Our areas of expertise span forecasting, planning, optimization, data analytics, and reporting. We deliver our vision using operations research, data science, and program management — and we continue to challenge the status quo, invent and simplify, and deliver excellence for our customers.

The NSP team is on a transformation journey. We are building a future-ready team that combines analytical rigor with AI fluency, executive-level communication, and the ability to drive outcomes across organizational boundaries. We are seeking an Senior Network Performance Analyst – AI Transformation to join this team and help shape how Amazon plans, staff, and optimizes its Customer Service network.

Basic qualifications

- 5+ years of program or project management experience
- 5+ years of supply chain experience
- Experience using data and metrics to determine and drive improvements
- Experience owning program strategy, end to end delivery, and communicating results to senior leadership

Preferred qualifications

- 2+ years of driving process improvements experience
- Master's degree, or MBA in business, operations, human resources, adult education, organizational development, instructional design or related field

title: Technical Program Manager, Field Integration & Testing, Amazon Leo
descriptionHtml:
Amazon Leo is Amazon's low Earth orbit satellite network. Our mission is to deliver fast, reliable broadband connectivity to customers beyond the reach of existing networks. From households to small businesses, schools, hospitals, and government agencies, Amazon Leo will serve communities and organizations operating in places without dependable internet access.

Within the Experience Validation organization, the Field Integration and Testing (FIT) team pioneers end-to-end network field validation—testing Leo's full signal path from the customer terminal through gateway infrastructure to the internet, in real customer environments that labs cannot fully replicate. We are looking for a Technical Program Manager to drive the execution of FIT's core testing operations and its international expansion as Leo scales across territories and new hardware. You will be the connective tissue between FIT, Leo engineering, the Beta teams, and the Amazon Devices Field Quality Engineering (FQE) partnership, keeping test coverage aligned with a fast-moving release cadence of new customer terminals, firmware, and mobile app builds.

Key job responsibilities
Own fleet management of remote Solution Labs across the Americas and EMEA, a core FIT workstream that keeps automated testing and verification infrastructure operational for engineering and product teams. Manage and modify AWS container-based workloads to meet evolving test requirements while maintaining security bar. Coordinate execution of country-specific functional test cases (regional IP routing, KPOP routing, Legal Interception) and B2B use cases across Solution Labs. Drive dependencies end-to-end, including Beta Ops provisioning, hardware delivery, and spot enablement. TPM-found issues with relevant stakeholders, manage schedules, risks, and open items, and maintain data-backed status reporting for leadership. Support Solution Lab and demo center expansion into future markets.

Success in this role requires strong technical program management judgment, comfort with networking and connectivity concepts, and the ability to coordinate many moving parts across teams, vendors, and geographies. You will define and report the metrics that show testing is on track and you anticipate dependencies and risks before they slip. You will write and communicate crisp and concise updates The ideal candidate is a hands-on, highly organized TPM who thrives in ambiguity, is comfortable working closely with engineers and field testers on production hardware and real integrations, and is energized by the challenge of proving out a brand-new satellite connectivity experience country by country.

Export Control Requirement:
Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

Basic qualifications

- 3+ years of technical product or program management experience
- 3+ years of project management disciplines including scope, schedule, budget, quality, along with risk and critical path management experience
- Experience managing programs across cross functional teams, building processes and coordinating release schedules
- Working knowledge of networking or connectivity concepts (e.g., IP routing, DNS, DHCP, latency, packet loss, VPN)

Preferred qualifications

- 3+ years of working directly with engineering teams experience
- Experience in satellite, telecommunications, wireless/RF, networking, or other connectivity/hardware domains
- Experience managing test, integration, verification, or field-testing programs involving physical hardware and third-party equipment
- Experience with defect/bug management processes and driving issues to resolution with engineering teams
- Experience coordinating lab operations or distributed field testing across multiple countries
- Familiarity with regulatory/compliance verification (e.g., lawful interception, RF compliance) or B2B/enterprise connectivity (AWS Direct Connect, enterprise routers)
- Experience standing up or scaling operational programs into new international regions
- Experience defining Go/No-Go or launch-readiness frameworks

descriptionHtml:

With AWS you can requisition compute power, storage, and many other services – gaining access to a suite of elastic IT infrastructure services as your business demands them. AWS is the leading platform for designing and developing applications for the cloud and is growing at a staggering pace in terms of revenue, customers, people, and complexity.
Reporting to the ASEAN Partner Leader, the Country Partner Leader owns the entire partner business and strategy for the Philippines and Vietnam. The Country Partner Leader is accountability for the entire partner landscape in the countries they cover, building a partner landscape plan that supports the AWS AGS Leaders strategic priorities and strategies to build the capabilities and capacity we need in our country partner landscape to support the growth priorities for AWS AGS country plans. This is a uniquely integrated role that brings together partner development and partner sales under a single leader responsible for driving revenue growth for AWS by driving new workloads on AWS with partners across identification to launch to delivery by building partner capability and accelerating co-sell across all partner types. They own our partner attach new launch workload goals, marketplace contract signing, AI and large migrations wins won through and with partners.
The role directly manages a team of Partner Sales Managers (PSMs), anchored on our largest customer opportunities, and Partner Development Managers (PDMs) managing our ISV and SI partners anchored on our most important partnerships. The leader also serves as the virtual leader of a broader in-country team including Partner Solution Architects (PSA), Distributor PDMs, Partner Development Representatives (PDR), and Specialists.
The successful candidate must be a proven leader who combines deep partner network expertise with strong sales execution. They will draw upon experience in account management, practice development, go-to-market solution positioning, relationship building, and working in both a direct and matrix operating structure. The individual must have deep experience managing a broad set of partners that are local and global from cloud-native start-ups and large system integrators to ISVs, consulting and advisory firms, value added resellers, distributors, and specialist solution providers.


Key job responsibilities
Strategy & Workload Growth
• Drive new workloads on AWS with partners, accelerate customer adoption of strategic and foundational workloads through APN consulting and technology partners via AWS Originated (AO), Partner Originated (PO), and Marketplace motions.
• Define and execute the unified country partner strategy spanning SI, ISV, MSP, VAR, and Distributor across the full partner lifecycle: recruitment, onboarding, enablement, solution build, go-to-market, and co-sell.
• Lead with industry solutions and GenAI, ensure partners build and deliver industry-specific, AI-enabled solutions that drive measurable business outcomes for customers. Champion the adoption of AWS AI services across the partner ecosystem.
• Scale AWS Marketplace adoption, drive ISV and consulting partner transaction volume through Marketplace, including Consulting Partner Private Offers (CPPO), PPA demand plans, and customer Marketplace commitments. Position Marketplace as the primary route to market for partner solutions.

Team Leadership
• Lead and develop the direct team of PSMs and PDMs (ISV & SI), setting priorities, coaching for performance, and ensuring alignment between partner sales and partner development activities.
• Serve as virtual leader of the broader in-country partner team, PSA, Distributor PDM, PDR, and Specialists ensuring all partner-facing resources are aligned to country priorities and operating as one cohesive team.

Co-Sell & Pipeline Execution
• Drive co-sell execution: shape deals early in the sales cycle, accelerate pipeline progression, align the right partners to strategic and foundational workloads, and unlock new Line of Business personas in customer accounts.
• Architect customer-partner strategy, act as a trusted advisor aligning ISVs and G/SIs to high-priority customer workloads and industry use cases, shaping customers’ long-term partner ecosystems.
• Orchestrate cross-functional resources (PSA, COE, CSM, MAP BD) to drive sales velocity, remove blockers, and maximize revenue realization across the partner portfolio.

Relationship Management & Governance
• Manage strategic partner C-level relationships across a wide range of key partners, establishing the country partner team as the single point of contact for partnership management and growth.
• Own forecast accuracy and operational cadence, lead MBR/QBR rhythm with partners and AWS country sales leadership, providing deep-dive insights into partner pipeline health and business performance.
• Collaborate with AWS country leadership and represent AWS at industry and partner events to deliver thought leadership and strengthen the AWS partner brand in-market.

- 10+ years of building and leading large teams and working in matrixed operating structures experience
- 7+ years of Go-To-Market, Business Development, Sales, or Consulting experience
- Bachelor's degree or equivalent
- Experience working and communicating with multiple stakeholders, C-level executives and cross functional teams or equivalent

title: Business Analyst II, Vendor Performance, OTS-GSP-TOPS
descriptionHtml:
Technology Operations & Partner Services (TOPS) manages $27M+ in annual vendor spend across 12+ technology service vendors and processes across 30K annual contacts that support Worldwide Grocery Stores (WWGS), which includes 549+ Whole Foods Market stores. Today, vendor performance is tracked reactively through manual reporting, creating blind spots that surface only after SLA breaches impact stores. This role eliminates that gap.

As the Business Analyst II, Vendor Performance, you will build and own the single source of truth for vendor performance across all TOPS programs — POS (NCR/Toshiba), Retail Scales (Bizerba), Depot (Denali/Truno), Smart Hands (Unisys/TechNet/Truno), Print Services (FlexPrint/Solum), In-Store Audio/Visual (Mood Media), and Finance Management 3P. You will extract, model, and analyze ServiceNow ticket data, vendor SLA metrics, and financial performance to deliver predictive visibility that enables proactive vendor accountability rather than reactive escalation.

This is not a reporting role. You will define the analytical frameworks that determine how TOPS measures vendor success, identify performance trends before they become store-impacting incidents, and provide the data foundation that drives process improvements and vendor negotiations. If you thrive on turning ambiguous data into actionable insight and want your analysis to directly influence multi-million-dollar vendor decisions, this is your role.

Key job responsibilities
Data Acquisition & Infrastructure
• Maintain automated data pipelines from ServiceNow (incident tasks, SLAs, work orders) to create a unified vendor performance data model across all vendors. Escalate and resolve data integrity defects.
• Own the TOPS vendor performance data architecture — define what we measure, how we measure it, among established sources of truth.
• Establish data quality standards and validation mechanisms for vendor-reported metrics vs. TOPS-measured actuals.

Analysis & Insight
• Optimization TOPS Vendor Scorecard: Support the composite scoring model program (Strategic, Efficiency, Tech Health pillars) applied consistently across all vendors.
• Develop predictive models that identify vendors trending toward SLA breach 2-4 weeks before store impact — shifting TOPS from reactive to preventive.
• Conduct root cause analysis on vendor performance deviations (regional patterns, seasonal trends, equipment-type correlations).
• Deliver monthly vendor performance narratives with actionable recommendations that directly inform Quarterly Business Reviews and vendor negotiations.
• Quantify the cost impact of vendor underperformance (missed SLAs → store downtime → revenue impact) to support contract enforcement.

Communication & Influence
• Present vendor performance insights to Leadership in narrative format, translating complex data into clear business implications.
• Partner with Vendor Programs Lead and individual Program Managers to ensure data drives vendor accountability conversations.
• Build self-service dashboards and automated reports that reduce manual reporting burden across the TOPS team.
• Influence vendor contract terms by providing irrefutable performance evidence during renewal negotiations.


A day in the life
Your morning starts with the automated vendor performance dashboard refreshing overnight data. You notice Bizerba's resolution times in the Southeast trending upward — your predictive model flags a likely SLA breach in 10 days if the pattern continues. You draft the insight narrative and send it to the Program Manager before the vendor even knows there's a problem. Mid-morning, you're refining the TOPS Vendor Scorecard methodology with the Vendor Programs Lead and Scorecard Program Manager, adding a new cost-per-resolution metric that will sharpen next quarter's contract negotiations. After lunch, you're building a new QuickSight dashboard that gives PMs self-service access to their vendor's real-time performance data — eliminating 4 hours of weekly manual reporting. You close the day presenting a root cause analysis to leadership: a pattern of NCR technician no-shows in three markets discovered by the Opportunities Program is costing $18K/month in extended downtime, and you have the data to enforce contractual remedies.

About the team
Our Organization: Our team sits in the OTS organization under Global Strategic Planning, focused on the technology vendor ecosystem that powers Whole Foods Market operations at scale. We ensure that third-party partners deliver the service quality, reliability, and cost efficiency that our stores depend on.

Our Culture: TOPS operates with a bias for action and an insistence on the highest standards. We are a data-driven team that values direct communication, intellectual honesty, and constructive disagreement. We celebrate people who challenge assumptions, bring evidence to the table, and hold each other accountable. We don't wait for permission — we identify problems, propose solutions, and execute.

Leadership Style: The hiring manager leads with directness and high autonomy. You will be given clear strategic direction and the freedom to define your own analytical approach — but you are expected to own outcomes fully, push back when you see a better path, and deliver insights that move the business. When blockers arise, they are addressed head-on — escalated quickly, resolved decisively, and never left to fester.

Expectations: Operate independently. Deliver measurable impact. Hold vendors accountable through irrefutable data. Your analysis will directly inform multi-million-dollar decisions — own that responsibility.

Basic qualifications

- 5+ years of Excel (including VBA, pivot tables, array functions, power pivots, etc.) and data visualization tools such as Tableau experience
- Experience defining requirements and using data and metrics to draw business insights
- Experience making business recommendations and influencing stakeholders
- Experience with data visualization using Tableau, Quicksight, or similar tools
- Experience working with ITSM platforms (ServiceNow preferred) and extracting/modeling ticket-level data

Preferred qualifications

- Experience with supplier or vendor relationship management
- Experience statistical modeling, or related analytic techniques
- 7+ years of retail or operations, or 5+ years of retail or operations experience
- Knowledge of statistical software such as R, Python
- Experience in applying statistical models for large-scale application and building automated analytical systems
- Understanding of contract structures, SLA frameworks, and vendor governance models

title: Applied Scientist - Amazon Robotics, Amazon Robotics - Vulcan Stow
descriptionHtml:
Our team in Amazon Robotics builds robotic systems that perform contact-rich manipulation tasks safely and reliably in complex, unstructured environments — at Amazon scale. Our scientists and engineers push the boundaries of robotic manipulation to handle enormous object diversity, bringing deep expertise across planning, control, perception, and machine learning. We learn from real-world data at a scale that few teams in robotics can access.

We are seeking an Applied Scientist to join our Motion Behaviors team. You will drive the development of learned controllers and manipulation behaviors, applying techniques like reinforcement learning and behavior cloning to robots operating in Amazon fulfillment centers. These problems remain unsolved at scale: our robots must improve continuously in environments where simulation alone is insufficient. You will make principled decisions about when learned approaches should replace engineered solutions, and how to select behaviors based on estimated risk. You will collaborate across disciplines and leverage rich operational data to continuously improve system performance.


Key job responsibilities
• Develop learned controllers and manipulation behaviors, from research prototyping through deployment on production robots.
• Research, design, and implement motion planning, control, and decision-making algorithms that improve the performance of deployed systems.
• Design and deploy learning pipelines that take policies from simulation training to reliable, real-time execution on physical robots.
• Develop models that predict manipulation outcomes and inform behavior selection under uncertainty.
• Leverage operational data from deployed systems to systematically identify failure modes and drive policy improvements.
• Represent Amazon in academia through publications and scientific presentations.

A day in the life
Amazon offers a full range of benefits that assist you and eligible family members, including domestic partners. Benefits can vary by location, the number of regularly scheduled hours you work, length of employment, and job status such as seasonal or temporary employment. The benefits that generally apply to regular, full-time employees include:
1. Medical, Dental, and Vision Coverage
2. Maternity and Parental Leave Options
3. Paid Time Off (PTO)
4. 401(k) Plan

If you are not sure that every qualification on the list above describes you exactly, we'd still love to hear from you! At Amazon, we value people with unique backgrounds, experiences, and skillsets. If you’re passionate about this role and want to make an impact on a global scale, please apply!

Basic qualifications

- PhD, or Master's degree and 4+ years of science, technology, engineering or related field experience
- Experience programming in Java, C++, Python or related language
- Experience in patents or publications at top-tier peer-reviewed conferences or journals
- Experience training reinforcement learning or imitation learning policies for manipulation or robot control problems
- Strong background in reinforcement learning, including reward design and training at scale in simulation

Preferred qualifications

- Experience in professional software development
- Experience with sim-to-real transfer (domain randomization, system identification, etc.), including transferring learned policies onto physical robots.
- Familiarity with learned dynamics or world models for manipulation

title: Software Development Engineer, AWS Quick
descriptionHtml:
Amazon Quick is building an AI-native work surface that understands what users want to accomplish and figures out how to get it done. We are looking for a Software Development Engineer III to design and deliver the third-party integrations that connect Quick to the business systems users rely on every day, enabling AI agents to take real action on their behalf. You will lead technical strategy for these connectors, working across teams to solve problems where requirements are clear but the right architecture is not. If you enjoy building systems that must work reliably at enterprise scale and want your code to directly drive product adoption, this is a role where your engineering decisions will have visible impact.


Key job responsibilities
Design and deliver third-party integrations and real-time connectors that enable AI agents within Quick to take action on behalf of users across the business systems they depend on.
Own the architectural direction for your team's integration platform, evaluating tradeoffs in scalability, performance, security, and maintainability while influencing technical decisions in systems you depend on but do not control.
Write high-quality code that sets the standard for your team in organization, clarity, error handling, and documentation, and drive adoption of consistent engineering practices.
Mentor and coach engineers on your team and across partner teams, contributing to hiring, career development, and a strong engineering culture.
Identify opportunities to simplify existing systems, reduce technical debt, and apply generative AI tools where they improve productivity and product quality.

A day in the life
You might start your morning reviewing a design for a new connector that links Quick to an external business application, offering feedback that strengthens the approach before implementation begins. Later, you pair with engineers on a partner team to align on an API contract and discuss how agents will authenticate and act within a third-party system. In the afternoon, you write code for a critical integration component, balancing near-term delivery with long-term extensibility. Between deep technical work, you check operational dashboards, refine runbooks, and spend time coaching a teammate through a tricky problem.


About the team
The Quick team is on a mission to build an AI-native work surface where users simply express what they want to accomplish and Quick handles the rest, drawing on deep knowledge of the user, their team, and their organization. Our real-time connectors are central to that vision: they drive adoption by giving Quick the breadth and reliability enterprises demand. We value collaboration, technical rigor, and open dialogue. If you want to join an inclusive team where your work directly shapes how people interact with AI at work, we would love to talk.

- 2+ years of non-internship design or architecture (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience
- 1+ years of software development engineer or related occupational experience
- 1+ years of designing and developing large-scale, multi-tiered, multi-threaded, embedded or distributed software applications, tools, systems, and services using: C#, C++, Java, or Perl experience
- 1+ years of Object Oriented Design experience
- Bachelor's degree or foreign equivalent in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, or a related field
- Experience programming with at least one software programming language

Preferred qualifications

- 3+ years of full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations experience
- Bachelor's degree in computer science or equivalent

title: Fuel Delivery Manager
descriptionHtml:
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

Role Summary:

Amazon is looking for a results-oriented individual to join the AWS Energy Team as an Fuel Delivery Manager. In this role, you will support AWS’s infrastructure expansion by leading natural gas infrastructure projects that supply fuel to large-scale natural gas generation facilities across AWS regions. This role will collaborate with internal and external stakeholders to deliver reliable, cost-effective natural gas supply to power AWS data centers.

The candidate must be able to manage the execution of multiple large-scale natural gas infrastructure projects across different US geographies. The candidate will manage interactions with gas utilities, pipeline operators, and local distribution companies (LDCs), and work with internal and external engineering, real estate, and planning teams to deliver gas infrastructure to serve AWS campuses. This includes but is not limited to managing EPC vendors, gas utility interconnects, metering and regulation stations (M&R), and pipeline laterals to meet AWS’s needs. The candidate will work as part of an integrated team to implement fuel program requirements and deliver tangible reliability and cost-saving results.

The ideal candidate will possess a strong natural gas infrastructure background and a proven track record of permitting, constructing, and commissioning gas pipelines, interconnects, and related facilities. The candidate will have experience working with gas utilities, pipeline operators, and regulatory agencies to develop, permit, contract, and deliver natural gas infrastructure. The right candidate will have a demonstrated ability to think strategically about business, operations, and technical challenges, with the skill set to drive tactical execution of project schedules, contracts, initiatives, and team goals. By establishing and growing business and technical relationships, and managing day-to-day interactions with these partners, you will be responsible for ensuring the fuel infrastructure requirements needed to support AWS’s global infrastructure expansion are met.

A key focus of this role is proactively identifying and flagging risks to natural gas delivery schedules and ensuring those risks are communicated and mitigated in a manner that informs overall datacenter delivery timelines.

This role requires domestic travel (up to 20%).


Key job responsibilities
• Manage multiple EPC vendors, gas utilities, pipeline operators, and Owner’s Engineers to deliver a portfolio of in-flight natural gas infrastructure projects including pipelines, laterals, metering and regulation (M&R) stations, and interconnect facilities.
• Oversee the permitting, construction, and commissioning of natural gas infrastructure to ensure on-time delivery aligned with datacenter commissioning schedules.
• Proactively identify, flag, and mitigate risks to project schedules, communicating impacts to datacenter delivery timelines to internal stakeholders.
• Manage capital budgets for natural gas infrastructure projects.
• Collaborate with internal teams and gas utilities on the implementation and management of fuel infrastructure projects in a timely and accurate fashion.
• Coordinate project schedule and risks with internal teams to ensure data center build timeline is informed by gas delivery.
• Identify and develop innovative cost-saving projects and initiatives related to natural gas infrastructure and supply.
• Work with gas utility regulators, pipeline operators, and permitting agencies to develop policies and guidelines that enable broader AWS strategies and objectives.


A day in the life
Our team is accountable for the full lifecycle of energy delivery to existing and future AWS data centers throughout North and South America. We are uniquely positioned and encouraged to execute innovative energy solutions that accelerate our sustainability goals, improve reliability, and optimize costs.

Our team is dedicated to supporting new team members in an environment that celebrates knowledge sharing and mentorship. Projects and tasks are assigned in a way that leverages your strengths and helps you further develop your skill set. title: Area Manager
descriptionHtml:
Operations is the beating heart of Amazon. This key part of our business makes sure we fulfil and dispatch orders efficiently so that our customers get their items on time. As an Area Manager, you’ll make sure your site is running as smoothly as it should so that we can meet customer demand. You will be leading a team that helps keep our operations safe, efficient, and of a high quality and taking on a number of projects across our network to drive productivity.



Key job responsibilities
- Create, oversee, and drive a culture of safety and wellbeing
- Analyse and implement changes to keep quality and productivity at a consistently high level
- Oversee projects to streamline processes, optimise productivity and increase quality of service for customers within your area of responsibility
- Analyse shift performance against relevant business objectives, and put in place actions to improve our operational excellence
- Work collaboratively with management-level colleagues to standardise shift practices

A day in the life
You’ll work on a shift pattern at one of our sites, making sure it is as productive as it can be. Your main focus will be to own and drive a culture of safety and uphold quality and shift performance standards. You’ll also oversee process improvements within your area and drive implementation. A typical day is varied, including everything from routine team management and daily operational responsibilities to process improvement and wide-scale operational contingency tasks. You’ll also be a role model and mentor to new managers.



About the team
Customer Fulfilment, or CF, is where it all started for Amazon. CF has scaled up from a humble team of booksellers to a sophisticated global team which handles more than 1.5 million orders every day. The team is the foundation of our business and its efforts have helped us diversify across new regions and services. With the help of emerging technology, we’re always looking for ways to offer a bigger, better product range – delivered quickly and affordably.

The CF team are the first people in the chain that helps customers get products at the speed we’re known for. We’re based in Fulfilment Centres, which are at the heart of Amazon’s fast-paced Operations network. Our centres are sometimes referred to as the ‘First Mile’ because it’s where most Amazon packages start their journey. We help to manage dynamic inventory and facilitate speedy deliveries round the clock.

Lots of different people work in our Fulfilment Centres, so there are plenty of opportunities for every skillset. Some of us work with physical products, while others analyse data to help everyone across the business make smart decisions.

Basic qualifications

- Advanced degree, or Bachelor's degree
- Experience managing people
- Experience communicating clearly and concisely with leadership, stakeholders, and cross-functional teams
- Experience using data to influence business decisions
- Advanced proficiency in verbal and written English and local language

Preferred qualifications

- Knowledge of Lean, Six Sigma and Kaizen techniques
- Experience in warehouse operations and logistics or equivalent
- Experience working with the MS Office suite (Word, Excel, Outlook) in a professional environment

title: Network Development Engineer II, AWS Internet Edge
descriptionHtml:
Do you like to use network and Unix systems engineering to deliver simple, sustainable and repeatable solutions? Would you like your work to play a key role in driving the stability and sustainability of next-generation IP networks?

AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

The AWS GCNA (Global Connectivity and Network Availability) Organization is looking for a Network Development Engineer to join our EDGE team. Network Development Engineers partner with our broader Infrastructure organization on configurations standards and tools, and collaborate with Systems and Software Engineers to ensure fast, smooth roll-out of new designs and products, and also deploy and sustain networking software tools.

AWS GCNA (Global Connectivity and Network Availability) is the backbone that connects the global AWS network. Focused on managing the internet traffic that allows users to access their information and applications regardless of where they are in the world. GCNA is responsible for building and designing a complex backbone network that allows internet traffic to flow efficiently between data centers and customers.


Key job responsibilities
Network Development Engineers perform high quality network and/or systems operations, deployments, scaling, technology refresh, sustaining engineering, best practices application, optimization, internal/external customer interactions, and produce appropriate technical documentation.
• Create and implement changes on the network.
• Work closely with our automation teams in defining the tools that allow us to scale at higher volume.
• Lead network projects in the areas of network sustaining engineering, network deployment/implementation, network scaling, technology refresh, best practices application, and/or network optimization.
• Sustain Amazon Web Services’ next generation networks for significant AWS customers by providing critical network support to diagnose, mitigate impact, and resolve large-scale networking events.
• Operate and troubleshoot network routing, interconnectivity, platforms, performance, and configurations issues; including necessary low level application interaction, Unix systems, and new age networking software tools.
• Drive and support innovation from Top of Rack to the Network Border and everything in between.
• Partner with our broader Network/Infrastructure organization in the areas of network engineering, configurations standards, and tools.
• Work closely with our Network/Systems/Software Engineering teams to ensure fast, smooth roll-out of new designs and products, as well as assist with deployment and sustaining of networking software tools.
• Maintain standards across the networking toolset and ensure that we are fully compliant to those standards and policies.
• Deliver simple, sustainable and repeatable solutions and processes.
• Collaborate with highest tier escalation engineers/resolvers.
• Create and review documentation and process regarding network implementation/deployments, recurring issues, new standard operating procedures, knowledge transfer material, etc.


A day in the life
Engineers in the Internet Edge organization have a wide range of responsibilities: we evolve routing policy, implement traffic engineering solutions, grow our peering footprint, secure the “front door” from bad actors on the Internet, and architect the hardware platforms and network design to support any Amazon product that needs to reach end-users worldwide. Our infrastructure moves terabits of traffic to and from the Internet at any given moment, and represents one of the largest edge surface areas in the world, requiring complex solutions to ensure that capacity always stays ahead of demand. To accomplish that, our engineers develop automation, write software, and work with a wide range of partner teams to continually improve and automate our Internet connectivity in areas such as capacity delivery, configuration deployment, impairment detection, and traffic optimization. Internet Edge engineers make decisions on both a day-to-day and long-term strategic basis, which carry a large amount of responsibility and impact across all of Amazon’s products.
• Work in a 24x7 team on call rotation, with ability to drive into workplace for critical events/needs.
• Manage customers during problem resolution and operating efficiently under pressure.
• Sit at the computer during scheduled work hours with appropriate breaks while maintaining a high level of alertness and attention to detail.
• Travel to data center/network sites and Amazon/customer offices as needed.


About the team
Internet Edge provides high-performing Internet connectivity for a wide range of use cases, such as retail (amazon.com), video streaming (Prime Video), content delivery (CloudFront), DNS (Route53), AWS services (such as EC2/S3), consumer devices (such as FireTV/Kindle/Echo), and more.

Within AWS Networking, the Internet Edge organization is responsible for connecting Amazon to the global Internet. With connections to thousands of unique external networks in hundreds of locations across the world, our mission is to deliver an Internet connectivity experience that sets the global standard for performance, availability, security, and cost, making Amazon the clear choice for our customers’ needs.

Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. title: Senior Product Manager
descriptionHtml:
Help shape how Whole Foods Market merchants plan, forecast, and make decisions, and put AI-powered tools in their hands to do it better. As a Senior Product Manager, you'll own the product strategy for intelligent automation, next-generation forecasting models, and the data foundations that connect them. You'll work at the intersection of AI/ML, merchant experience, and supply chain data to build capabilities that fundamentally change how category managers operate across one of the world's most trusted grocery brands.

Whole Foods Market is known as the number one grocer suppliers want to be in, and our merchants are central to that reputation. Your job is to make them faster, sharper, and more confident in their decisions, whether that's through AI agents that surface insights at the point of decision, forecasting models that replace legacy planning systems, or data integrations that give merchants end-to-end visibility from supplier to shelf. You'll partner closely with engineering, UX research, analytics, and business teams spanning Amazon and WFM to translate complex technical capabilities into tools merchants trust and adopt.

Key job responsibilities
Own the product strategy and roadmap for AI-powered merchant intelligence tools, including adoption strategy, capability governance, and merchant enablement

Lead cross-functional execution of forecasting model migration: defining success criteria, orchestrating data readiness, managing cross-team dependencies, and driving go/no-go decisions

Drive data integration and catalog harmonization initiatives across multiple systems and organizations, resolving complex upstream and downstream dependencies

Define product requirements for new analytical capabilities, including store clustering, category intelligence, and assortment optimization, from problem framing through OP1 commitment

Earn merchant trust through direct engagement: translating technical capabilities into business value, validating solutions in the field, and building feedback loops that inform the roadmap

Navigate a complex stakeholder landscape spanning product, engineering, supply chain, UX, and merchandising organizations across both Amazon and Whole Foods Market

A day in the life
You'll move between strategic planning and hands-on execution in a single day. One hour you're reviewing AI capability adoption trends and refining the product roadmap, the next you're in a cross-functional sync resolving data dependencies with engineering and analytics partners. After lunch, you might walk category managers through a new capability prototype, then pivot to a UX research debrief that reshapes how you think about the planning workflow. You'll regularly translate between technical ML conversations and practical merchant needs. Expect to partner with teams across Amazon and WFM, navigate ambiguity, and drive clarity where there isn't any yet.

About the team
Our team builds the tools and platforms that Whole Foods Market category managers rely on to plan, price, promote, and merchandise products. Our portfolio spans assortment planning, pricing optimization, promotions planning, and space and merchandising execution, all powered by a shared data foundation and increasingly driven by AI. We're at an inflection point: transitioning from legacy planning systems to intelligent, data-driven capabilities that change how merchants work. We build in close partnership with Amazon's retail, technology, and operations teams. We move fast, operate with high ambiguity, and value PMs who earn trust with both engineers and merchants.

- 5+ years of product or program management, product marketing, business development or technology experience
- Bachelor's degree or equivalent
- Experience as a product manager or owner
- Experience owning feature delivery and tradeoffs of a product
- Experience in influencing senior leadership through data driven insights

Preferred qualifications

- Experience owning/driving roadmap strategy and definition
- Usage of generative AI tools to enhance workflow efficiency, with a willingness to learn effective prompting and evaluation practices.

title: Senior Industrial Designer
descriptionHtml:
We are seeking a Senior Industrial Designer to translate design vision into production-ready form language for our next-generation robotic platforms. You will own form development from early volumetric exploration through surface refinement — defining what our robots look and feel like while ensuring designs are manufacturable from the start. You’ll work at the intersection of aesthetics and engineering, balancing proportion, character, and visual brand coherence with the realities of complex electromechanical packaging, dynamic articulation, and production tooling.

Key job responsibilities
- Form Development & Surface Refinement: Explore, iterate, and refine complex multi-part robotic enclosures, articulating fairings, and structural chassis using Rhino, SubD, Alias, or Blender — from rapid volumetric studies through production-intent surfacing with Class-A quality standards.
- Design for Manufacturing: Incorporate draft angles, parting line strategy, wall thickness constraints, and tooling considerations into the design process from the start. Develop surfaces with production intent across injection molding, sheet metal, die casting, and composite fabrication processes.
- Unified Design Language: Establish and maintain a cohesive visual brand language across the entire robot — ensuring seamless aesthetic and proportional transitions between static and moving components.
- Dynamic Articulation & Clearances: Explore and resolve how physical panels interact, reveal internal mechanisms, and clear dynamic ranges of motion while maintaining design intent.
- Component Packaging & Integration: Collaborate closely with mechanical engineering, robotics, and manufacturing teams to package high-density motor assemblies, cooling systems, battery modules, and sensor arrays into an appealing, functional, and producible envelope.
- Engineering Handoff: Deliver organized, proportion-locked CAD models (SubD / clean NURBS / production-intent surfaces) with clear design intent documentation — character lines, highlight priorities, parting line intent, and DFM annotations ready for tooling development.

Basic qualifications

- 5+ years of industrial design experience with a focus on complex physical products (robotics, automotive, medical devices, consumer electronics, or similar electromechanical systems)
- Experience working directly with mechanical engineering and manufacturing engineering teams through production
- Bachelor’s degree in Industrial Design, Transportation Design, Product Design, or related field
- Expert-level proficiency in Rhino, SubD modeling, Alias, Blender, or Plasticity with demonstrated ability to develop refined surfaces efficiently
- Portfolio demonstrating exceptional sense of proportion, visual hierarchy, and unified aesthetic across complex, multi-component mechanical systems where multiple subsystems must integrate and interact
- Working knowledge of manufacturing processes including injection molding, sheet metal forming, die casting, and composite fabrication
- Understanding of dynamic kinematic clearances, packaging volumes for motors/electronics, and thermal management considerations
- Proven ability to maintain clean model organization, logical parting line intent, and deliver production-ready STEP/mesh files

Preferred qualifications

- Experience designing articulated or dynamic mechanical systems (robotics, automotive, powered equipment)
- Class-A surfacing skills in Alias or equivalent
- Experience taking designs from concept through tooling kickoff
- Background in automotive, surgical robotics, or consumer robotics design studios
- Familiarity with GD&T and tolerance stack-up considerations at the industrial design level
- Proficiency in Gravity Sketch, Vizcom AI, or other rapid visualization tools
- Experience with physical prototyping workflows (3D printing, CNC, soft tooling)

title: Risk Manager II, WWOS AMER Resilience
descriptionHtml:
** This position can be located out of any physical Amazon location in the U.S. **

Resiliency protects our People, Operations, Assets and brand. We do this by being embedded within the teams that move packages and serve customers every hour of every day. The WWOS Risk & Resilience organization exists because uninterrupted operations is not optional, it is the mission. To serve our customers we must bridge Risk and Operations, assessing threats and leading our business partners through Risk Working Groups and Crisis Management Team events with credibility and operational fluency. That means knowing our customers, understanding their constraints, and helping them manage risk in the context of their network reality. Making our customers more resilient through planning, risk mitigation, and automation is our mission.

As a Resilience Manager, you will design, build, and own the systems, frameworks, and programs that enable 24/7 operational continuity across Amazon's global network. This requires both the credibility to make real time decisions during live disruption events and the strategic discipline to design durable frameworks that prevent recurrence. Dynamic risk management and operational decision making are the primary competencies. Traditional resilience planning supports the operational mission.

You will drive delivery of multiple concurrent resilience and OC programs, own customer relationships with Operations, CX, Transport, S&LP, and cross functional partners, and influence the resilience agenda at senior leadership forums including briefing L10s on Daily Business Reviews (DBRs). You will independently translate complex operational and security challenges into scalable mitigations that protect Amazon's people, operations, assets, and brand.

We operate in a 24/7 environment so we operate a follow the sun model, ensuring that we support our team, regardless of region, to delight our customers. When ambiguous or systemic challenges arise, you exercise independent judgement to develop solutions, drive cross functional alignment, and ensure business continuity across the network. This role operates within globally defined frameworks while maintaining authority to adapt procedures to local regulatory and operational requirements.

Key job responsibilities
Category 1 —Risk Management & E2E Contingency Planning (40%)
Own the end-to-end contingency playbook portfolio for the assigned region/domain — from design through validated deployment, signing off on playbook quality before regional release.
Design and build E2E contingency playbooks covering capacity loss at origin and volume impediment to destination scenarios, defining activation thresholds, decision trees, and automated PRECOG trigger protocols.
Design and conduct comprehensive risk assessments and analytical deep dives to identify threats, vulnerabilities, and capability gaps across the assigned region.
Own dynamic risk escalation protocols — defining when and how risk signals from PRECOG, SEM Dashboard, and field intelligence translate into contingency activation.
Develop risk intelligence products, strategic threat assessments, and program performance reporting for senior stakeholders.
Shape the evolution of regional resilience strategy in partnership with the Regional Resilience Lead, identifying emerging risks and capability gaps proactively.
Drive real-time operational decision-making during disruption events, exercising independent judgement to activate, modify, or stand-down contingency responses.
Validate playbook effectiveness through post-event analysis, updating activation thresholds and decision trees based on operational reality.

Category 2 — Resilience Frameworks & Program Delivery (20%)
Design, implement, and own resilience frameworks, standards, and programs that enable consistent preparedness and response capabilities across the assigned scope.
Drive multiple concurrent programs and projects from concept through delivery, owning technology roadmap input and BRD prioritization for assigned domains.
Shape technology requirements and BRD development for operational systems (PRECOG, SEM Dashboard, Umbrella, and equivalent tools), coordinating cross-functional delivery with tech, ops, and CX partners.
Design and maintain program governance documentation including RACI matrices, decision logs, and status reporting across multiple concurrent deliverables.
Translate multiple concurrent resilience initiatives into prioritized, executable work with minimal direction from senior leadership.
Establish and monitor Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) to measure program performance, risk posture, and resilience maturity across assigned areas.
Drive continuous improvement of operational procedures and protocols through lessons learned, after-action reviews, and cross-functional best practice adoption.
Build organizational resilience by developing and implementing preparedness mechanisms for a range of events that pose risk to people, operations, assets, and brand.

Category 3 — Operational Response & Crisis Coordination (20%)
Lead coordination of large-scale/crisis events, emerging threats, and high-severity incident response efforts across multiple organizations to minimize operational disruption.
Own On-Call rotation responsibilities, responding to emerging threats with direct mitigation and recovery support to field teams.
Coordinate with GSOC on incident management activation, ensuring seamless handoff between monitoring, escalation, and crisis management protocols.
Make real-time operational decisions under uncertainty — activating, modifying, or standing down contingency responses based on evolving threat intelligence and operational data.
Lead after-action reviews and incident analyses, determining root causes, driving corrective actions, and implementing mechanisms to prevent recurrence.
Build organizational resilience by implementing preparedness mechanisms and ensuring field teams can execute response protocols under pressure.
Train, advise, and partner with other functions in identifying, managing, and mitigating risks through robust standards and processes.

Category 4 — Preparedness, Training & Exercising (10%)
Own the exercise program strategy for the assigned region/domain, designing and delivering train-the-trainer programs for GSOC OC Analysts on playbook execution.
Develop and facilitate exercises (tabletop, functional drills, full-scale simulations) to validate E2E contingency plans and resilience frameworks, owning readiness and certification rates within assigned scope.
Drive training curriculum development and quality assurance, shaping and maintaining SOPs, ERPs, and response documentation to operational excellence standards.
Build organizational resilience by developing and implementing preparedness mechanisms for a range of events that pose risk to people, operations, assets, and brand.

Category 5 — Stakeholder Engagement & Cross-Functional Influence (10%)
Build and maintain strategic partnerships with Regional S&LP, Operations, CX, Transport, Legal, and cross-functional business continuity stakeholders.
Own customer/stakeholder relationships at senior level (
L8+) and drive alignment across competing priorities.
Represent the Resilience Pillar at senior leadership forums, contributing regional insights and operational expertise to enterprise-wide resilience strategy.
Brief senior leadership (Director/VP level) with data-driven Daily Business Reviews (DBRs) and strategic recommendations.
Influence resilience outcomes aligned with organizational priorities without direct authority across diverse functional and cultural contexts.
Contribute regional insights and operational expertise to enterprise-wide resilience strategy and program development through global forums.

A day in the life
No two days look the same — but here is what a typical week looks like:

Morning: Review overnight disruption event reports and the regional threat landscape. Validate that automated protocols executed as designed; flag any playbook gaps identified during live events for the continuous improvement backlog. Independently assess emerging risks that could impact operations and brief the regional leadership team.
Mid-morning: Lead a cross-functional alignment call with Ops, CX, Transport, and S&LP partners to advance a new E2E contingency playbook for a high-risk disruption scenario. Resolve competing priorities across partner organizations. Conduct a complex risk assessment for an emerging threat, developing mitigation strategies and coordinating response options.
Afternoon: Drive a program governance review, updating RACI matrices and decision logs for concurrent technology and resilience deliverables. Coordinate with GSOC on incident management protocols. Engage senior stakeholders across Operations, S&LP, and Legal on resilience maturity gaps and remediation priorities.
Late afternoon: Facilitate a tabletop exercise with GSOC Analysts and field teams to test a recently deployed playbook; document findings and translate them into actionable improvement recommendations. Lead an after-action review for a recent crisis event, determining root causes and driving corrective actions.
End of week: Prepare executive briefing content for an L10 Daily Business Review (DBR); synthesize disruption data, playbook effectiveness metrics, and risk intelligence into decision-ready narratives. Develop and deliver risk intelligence products and strategic recommendations to senior stakeholders.
Follow the sun: During your on hours, respond to emerging threats with direct mitigation and recovery support. Lead coordination of large-scale/crisis events, making real-time operational decisions under uncertainty. Activate contingency plans and coordinate response across multiple organizations to minimize operational disruption.

About the team
The WWOS Risk & Resilience organization operates across seven pillars, each owning a distinct capability domain within Amazon's global operational risk architecture. The Resilience Pillar, where this role sits, owns the development, maintenance, and continuous improvement of operational continuity capabilities, resilience frameworks, and governance structures that enable 24/7/365 operational continuity and crisis management at network scale.

The Regional Resilience Team is the execution engine for both operational continuity program delivery and resilience strategy across assigned regional scope. The team works in close coordination with:
• Risk Management: Receiving escalations when risk exceeds intervention thresholds; translating risk signals into operational action
• GSOC: Coordinating incident management and crisis management activation; ensuring 24/7 operational coverage
• Risk Preparedness: Executing training and exercise programs; validating playbook readiness
• Regional S&LP: Partnering on security risk assessments and threat intelligence
• Operations, CX & Transport Leadership: Owning customer relationships and representing resilience at senior leadership forums

The team operates within globally defined frameworks while maintaining authority to adapt procedures to local regulatory and operational requirements. The role owns customer relationships with Ops, CX, S&LP, and Transport leadership partners, and represents the program at senior leadership forums including Daily Business Reviews (DBRs) with L10 stakeholders.

This is a team of operators turned program leaders. Hands on network knowledge is non-negotiable. The ability to make real time decisions under uncertainty, to understand how volume flows through the network, and to anticipate where disruption will propagate before it arrives. These are baseline expectations, not differentiators. If you come from consulting or traditional BCM without direct operational experience, you will need to demonstrate that you can operate at network speed, think in terms of packages and customers rather than frameworks and audits, and earn credibility with field teams who live the operation every day. We protect the machine from the inside. We do not advise it from the outside.

We measure success by what didn't break, what kept moving, how much impact was mitigated, and what recovered before the customer noticed. Every framework, every playbook, every risk assessment exists to serve one outcome: uninterrupted operations.

Basic qualifications

- 4+ years of compliance program management, legal, governance, audit, risk/loss prevention, or equivalent experience
- Bachelor's degree or equivalent
- Experience handling confidential information

Preferred qualifications

- 3+ years of program requirements definition and data and metrics leveraging to drive improvements experience
- Experience with SQL and Excel

title: Senior Capacity Delivery Reliability Planner , AWS Infra Supply Chain
descriptionHtml:
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

Are you ready to architect the digital backbone of tomorrow? We're seeking a Senior Supply Capacity Delivery Reliability Planner to lead end-to-end capacity and planning orchestration across strategic, enterprise, operational, and tactical levels in our global cloud infrastructure organization. This isn't just a job – it's your chance to directly influence how we scale and deliver the infrastructure powering the digital world.

The ideal candidate brings a proven track record of driving step-change capabilities and business process transformations in SIOP environments. They should have experience delivering tangible improvements in speed, accuracy, visibility, and cross-functional alignment. In this role, you will be a key architect in transforming critical aspects of our operations. Specifically, you will lead efforts to revolutionize how demand is captured, capacity is allocated, and infrastructure is built at a hyperscale level.


Key job responsibilities
Strategic Level: You will define and evolve multi-year cloud infrastructure strategies aligned with business growth, sustainability, and global risk trends. Leading cross-functional strategic capacity modeling to support emerging workloads (such as AI/ML and HPC) and future region expansions will be a crucial part of your role. Additionally, you'll drive long-term innovation in planning frameworks and digital planning tools to support dynamic business shifts.

Enterprise Level: Your responsibilities include delivering enterprise-wide SIOP transformations that break down silos between engineering, supply chain, finance, manufacturing, and infrastructure delivery. You'll design and implement scenario-based capacity planning, integrating hardware, power, land, and construction considerations. Establishing a resilient planning governance model with visibility from executive reviews to regional deployment readiness will also fall under your purview.

Operational Level: You'll be tasked with translating strategic demand into executable regional build and fulfillment plans, managing infrastructure readiness across supply constraints. Leading cross-regional planning standardization and continuous improvement efforts to reduce cycle time and increase delivery velocity will be essential. You'll also drive alignment between planning, sourcing, and manufacturing teams to ensure predictable outcomes.

Tactical Level: Your day-to-day responsibilities will include orchestrating the execution of plans and handling exceptions across global regions. You'll monitor fulfillment signals, adjust plans in real-time, and escalate barriers to delivery to ensure near-zero disruption. Deploying automation and advanced analytics to proactively identify and solve risks and bottlenecks will be a key aspect of your tactical duties.


About the team
Our team is dedicated to supporting new members. We have a broad mix of experience levels and tenures, and we’re building an environment that celebrates knowledge-sharing and mentorship.

Why AWS
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Diverse Experiences
Amazon values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Work/Life Balance
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.

Inclusive Team Culture
Here at AWS, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empower us to be proud of our differences. Ongoing events and learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) and AmazeCon (gender diversity) conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness.

Mentorship and Career Growth
We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree or equivalent in a related technical field
- Bachelor's degree in supply chain management, operations, engineering, analytics or related field
- 7+ years of technical infrastructure management experience
- Knowledge of best practices and emerging technologies, related to integrated planning, SIOP/IBP, or operations roles with global scope

Preferred qualifications

- Proven experience designing and executing SIOP transformations that resulted in measurable improvements in forecast accuracy, service levels, and delivery velocity.
- Background in demand planning, capacity planning, material planning, production planning etc. across multiple industries.
- Experience in cloud, hyperscale technology, or complex infrastructure supply chains.
- Proven success in leading business process transformation and implementing step-change planning capabilities across organizations.
- Advanced fluency in planning platforms and scenario modeling techniques.
- Strong business acumen and stakeholder influence — able to operate effectively from boardroom to build floor.
